tutorial_choice.rejected_reason: DPW4_Aircraft is the genuine wing-body(-tail) config (designSurfaces=[wing,tail,body]) but ships HPC-scale snappyHexMesh settings: surface refinement levels 9-12, maxGlobalCells=200,000,000, decomposeParDict numberOfSubdomains=192. Retuning 11 STL parts' refinement to fit a 75-minute box with no prior data point on this geometry was judged high-risk (multi-iteration snappyHexMesh quality tuning) and was not attempted -- so no data exists on whether it would have meshed successfully in-box.
tutorial_choice.chosen_reason: CRM_Wing has a single deterministic mesh pipeline (official pre-coarsened CGNS surface + one more cgns_utils coarsen + pyHyp hyperbolic extrusion, N=53 layers) already proven in this lab tonight on Onera M6 (A3). Deterministic cell count, no iterative mesh-quality tuning.
tutorial_choice.disclosed_limitation: CRM_Wing is wing-alone (designSurfaces=[wing] only, no fuselage/tail patch) -- this is honestly NOT a full wing-body reproduction. Disclosed, not hidden.

Its own log file was later overwritten by attempt 3's log via filename reuse; last known state before stop (captured in-session, not from a surviving log file): t=200, CD=0.03118, CL=0.4036.

wall_report.gradient_infeasibility_basis: A3 (Onera M6, same DARhoSimpleCFoam solver family) OOM'd the adjoint at 399,360 cells (18g cap) and again at 99,840 cells (8g cap) after 8 disclosed mitigations (2 memory caps, 2 rank counts, gmresRestart 1000->200, pcFillLevel 1->0) were ruled out. Root cause per A3: OpenMDAO's reverse-mode sweep for any requested total derivative unavoidably builds a mesh-sized d[residuals]/d[vol_coords] Jacobian block regardless of wrt=; this is structural, not fixable by mesh coarsening alone (a 4x cell cut in A3 only moved the OOM to a later pipeline stage).
wall_report.true_dpw_grid_scale_cells: 7.2 million (L0 coarse) per docs/DPW-CRM-SCOPING.md -- two further orders of magnitude beyond this mesh
wall_report.what_a_gradient_would_need: A host with materially more free RAM dedicated solely to this job with peak DAJacCon/DASolver RSS measured empirically first, OR DAFoam's untested adjUseColoring=False matrix-free path (trades memory for an unmeasured runtime cost). Neither attempted tonight.

lessons: The Bash tool's own `timeout` parameter is the only thing that reliably bounds a foreground `docker run` -- a shell-level `timeout N` wrapper does not help if the outer tool call itself times out first (default 120000ms); the outer kill detaches from but does not stop the container, producing exactly the kind of orphan the process rules warn against. Set the tool's timeout parameter explicitly and generously for every foreground solver launch.

Never `docker stop` a container mid-write of a checkpoint intended for resume -- it corrupts the field file being written and forces a clean restart. Cost here: ~0.8 core-min wasted plus the audit trail of attempt 1's log (overwritten by filename reuse on the restart) -- corrected by disclosure in this record rather than hidden.
net_effect_on_deliverable: None. The accepted primal is fully converged on every field below primalMinResTol=1e-8, reproduces DAFoam's own published tutorial baseline to 0.0067%, and total elapsed time (including the two discarded attempts) was ~14 minutes against a 75-minute time-box.
